title: Satoshi-era bitcoin faces a bigger quantum threat after Google’s new Willow breakthrough

content: Google’s new Willow quantum chip breakthrough has raised concerns for Satoshi-era bitcoin. The chip can prepare special quantum states for advanced calculations with significantly fewer errors. This technological advance reduces a major hardware bottleneck, potentially bringing future attempts to crack bitcoin wallets closer to reality.

title: Circle Targets 40 New Markets As USDC Push Moves Beyond Crypto Trading
summary: TL;DR: Circle plans to expand USDC infrastructure into approximately 40 developing and emerging markets. The company is targeting international payments and access to digital dollars rather than relying solely on cryptocurrency exchange demand. Circle is looking well beyond cryptocurrency trading as it prepares to extend USDC’s reach into approximately 40 emerging and developing markets. CEO Jeremy Allaire outlined the ambition during discussions surrounding the October 16 international financial meetings in Bangkok. The strategy focuses on places where businesses and individuals want access to dollar-denominated payments but may face expensive or inefficient conventional banking arrangements. The opportunity is straightforward: a stablecoin that can move between compatible wallets at any hour could offer a useful payment alternative. The difficult part is connecting those wallets to actual financial activity. From Exchange Balances To Everyday Payments USDC has long been widely used by cryptocurrency traders as a dollar-linked asset. Circle now wants to make it part of cross-border invoices, business settlement and consumer payments. That requires more than issuing tokens. Businesses need reliable local currency conversion, banking connections, compliance arrangements and confidence that USDC can be redeemed as intended. Circle has increasingly built partnerships around these services. Existing stablecoin initiatives, including creator payouts and digital payment programmes, show how digital dollars can be incorporated into familiar financial experiences. Expansion Will Be Uneven Regulation is likely to determine the pace of Circle’s international push. Some countries welcome stablecoin payment infrastructure, while others restrict foreign currency access or require substantial local licensing. Tether’s USDT is also already entrenched across a number of international markets. Circle must therefore establish the practical value of USDC for customers who may never buy Bitcoin or speculate on another cryptocurrency. title: Judge Rejects Gemini And CFTC Bid To Overturn $5 Million Settlement
summary: TL;DR: A federal judge has rejected a joint attempt by Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to overturn the exchange’s $5 million settlement. The decision leaves the existing judgment in place despite the regulator’s changed approach to cryptocurrency enforcement. Gemini has failed in an unusual attempt to undo a regulatory settlement, despite having the very agency that brought the original case on its side. US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein rejected a joint motion by the exchange and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission seeking to vacate a consent judgment entered in January 2025. The settlement arose from allegations that Gemini misled the regulator during its review of a proposed Bitcoin futures product in 2017. Gemini agreed to pay a $5 million penalty and accepted a permanent injunction. When Regulators Change Their Minds The CFTC subsequently reconsidered the original enforcement case as its digital asset priorities evolved. Together with Gemini, it asked the court to revisit the settlement. That is a very different situation from the more familiar legal battle in which an exchange disputes a regulator’s allegations. This time, both parties wanted relief from the court’s earlier judgment. But a change in enforcement policy does not automatically erase a final court order. The judge found that the arguments presented did not satisfy the legal standards for reopening the settlement. The decision is significant for other cryptocurrency businesses hoping that a more accommodating federal regulatory environment might undo historical enforcement outcomes. What Changes For Gemini? In the immediate term, very little. The settlement remains in effect and the court has not imposed a new fine. The wider message is more important: courts retain control of their judgments, even when a regulatory agency changes its view of a case. Washington’s approach to cryptocurrency may have become more favourable, but companies cannot assume that previously approved settlements will disappear alongside the political circumstances in which they were reached. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: A federal judge has rejected a joint motion by Gemini and the CFTC to overturn a $5 million settlement regarding 2017 Bitcoin futures. Despite both the exchange and the regulator agreeing to vacate the consent judgment following a shift in enforcement priorities, the court ruled that the legal standards for reopening the case were not met, keeping the original penalty in place.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $82 Million As BlackRock Leads Friday’s Withdrawals
summary: TL;DR: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $82.4 million in net outflows on October 16. BlackRock’s flagship spot Bitcoin ETF accounted for most of the selling as US-listed Bitcoin investment funds closed Friday’s session with net withdrawals of approximately $82.4 million. Farside Investors’ figures show that the iShares Bitcoin Trust, known as IBIT, lost $71.8 million on October 16. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund recorded around $10.6 million in net outflows, while the remaining products were broadly flat on the day. That concentration matters because IBIT has become one of the clearest measures of Bitcoin demand through traditional brokerage accounts. Another Uneven Week For ETF Demand The latest withdrawals followed substantial redemptions earlier in the week. October 14 saw roughly $261 million leave the category, followed by a modest return to net inflows on October 15. Friday’s negative session therefore suggests demand remains unsettled rather than following a clear trend. Investors have seen considerably larger individual outflow days in the past. Earlier October withdrawals approached $485 million in a single session, demonstrating how rapidly demand through these products can shift. Context Is Important An ETF outflow is not a complete measure of institutional Bitcoin ownership, and it does not necessarily indicate that every underlying holder has abandoned a long-term position. Net inflows into the US spot Bitcoin ETF market since the products launched remained substantial despite the latest withdrawals. The next trading sessions will be important. A quick recovery would suggest another temporary adjustment, while continued redemptions from IBIT and FBTC would place greater emphasis on whether traditional investors are reducing their exposure amid broader market uncertainty. Private investment products may impose selling restrictions, and their holdings can be considerably less liquid than publicly traded ETFs. The lower minimum also does nothing to eliminate the volatility of the cryptocurrencies inside each portfolio. Still, the arrangement provides another example of how traditional asset managers are attempting to make a wider variety of digital assets accessible through familiar investment structures. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Arbitrum Courts European Investors Managing €800 Billion With New Revenue Pitch
summary: TL;DR: Arbitrum representatives have presented the network’s infrastructure and revenue model to European financial institutions managing substantial assets. The meetings should not be confused with confirmed investment commitments to ARB. Arbitrum is increasingly pitching itself as a blockchain infrastructure business rather than simply another cryptocurrency ecosystem. During institutional meetings reported on October 16, representatives discussed the network’s commercial potential with European banks, wealth managers and other professional investors. The participating organisations were said to represent more than €800 billion in assets under management. That figure describes the institutions attending the presentations. It does not represent money invested in Arbitrum or its native token. Explaining The Business Behind The Blockchain The discussions placed particular emphasis on how blockchain infrastructure can earn fees through licensing, network services and support for financial applications. Research presented alongside WisdomTree material explored Arbitrum’s financial performance and the possibility of building sustainable revenue rather than relying on speculative token trading. Institutional projects using Arbitrum technology are one possible route toward such a model. They demonstrate how a financial business might adopt blockchain infrastructure without requiring its customers to trade ARB directly. Arbitrum’s community has also discussed new ways to generate revenue for its DAO treasury. Interest Is Not Adoption The meetings do not confirm that any participating bank has committed to deploy the technology, purchase tokens or establish a product. For Arbitrum, the next task is converting conversations into actual commercial integrations. Banks will demand clear answers about reliability, compliance, privacy and the economics of using blockchain rails. Still, the change in emphasis is notable. Blockchain companies increasingly want to be assessed on the value of the services they provide, not simply the price of their coins. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
